en: The Scripture of the Great Bright Dhāraṇī of the Invincible One,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao San Dafu,
Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, and Dharma-Teaching Master, the Subject [Name].
I take refuge and pay homage to the Perfectly Awakened One, the Dharma,
and the Noble Sangha. The Bodhisattva has spoken this vidyā-mantra,
which expounds the root mantra-method for destroying obstacles, vetālas, khaṭvāṅgas, and bhūtas.
This vidyā can destroy the malevolent rites performed by hosts of yakṣas and rākṣasas,
ensuring that right conduct is always maintained.
If there are sentient beings who, with earnest devotion and single-minded focus, receive and uphold this vidyā-mantra, [it shall protect them].
Whether written on silk cloth or on birch bark paper and the like,
in all such places, the various evil spirits and demons will give rise to resolute compassion.
It eliminates obstacles and calamities and accomplishes the most supreme matters.
If it is worn upon the neck when entering an army,
even if people are killing one another, it will be able to provide protection.
With a mind free from delusion and fear, not even a single hair will be harmed;
if one wears it upon one's arm, one will swiftly attain victory.
As the Buddha said:
If any man or woman upholds this vidyā, all their desires shall be accomplished.
Even if they are bound by the prohibitions of royal law, [they shall be released].
If one encounters the perils of lions, tigers, or wolves while traveling through a wilderness, or meets with bandits on the road,
this Great Mantra has the power to provide protection and deliverance.
It causes one to be free from all fears and to attain peace and happiness.
If any woman wears it upon her head and upholds it,
she will always have her retinue give rise to love and respect, and she will constantly obtain wealth and treasures.
Furthermore, for those who are pregnant and experience difficulties in childbirth, they shall quickly attain safety and peace.
This great vidyā-mantra spoken by the Bodhisattva shall likewise provide constant protection day and night at all times.
If there is a wise person who single-mindedly upholds this,
whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down,
they shall not be harmed by ghosts, demons, or any such calamities.
Even when one is intoxicated by alcohol or asleep, no evil dreams shall occur.
This is the "Invincible" vidyā;
if one holds it and recites it, [no harm shall come].
All quarrels and disputes among kings, villages, and the masses,
as well as all obstacles and hindrances, shall entirely dissipate. At that time,
the Bodhisattva Aparājita addressed the various māras, saying:
I shall now explain;
you hosts of bhūtas, listen to what I say.
The Bodhisattva beheld those armies of evil Māras.
Appearing before him with various forms and colors,
he spoke these words to those demonic armies:
"For many millions of eons, I have sought awakening."
Renouncing his own life, wife, children, and wealth,
he was able to perform what is difficult to do, practicing great diligence to bring benefit and peace to all sentient beings.
With his conduct and vows fulfilled, he dwelt at the Bodhi tree,
diligently upholding the realization of the true Dharma.
At that time, the Māra King led a host of evil armies and came to create obstacles.
By the power of the vidyā-mantra, they shall be subdued.
As I contemplate this, may those who were my demonic companions in the past rejoice in their defeat;
may my former enemies be destroyed by themselves.
I shall now proclaim the great vidyā-mantra for destroying the armies of Māra. It is as follows:
*Tadyathā | hulu hulu caṇḍe mātaṅgi svāhā*. When the Bodhisattva Aparājita spoke this mantra, [the hosts were subdued].
She transformed her body into the likeness of a celestial maiden (devī).
Standing before Māra, she gave rise to a heart of compassion and,
joining her palms above her head, spoke these words:
The Bodhisattva’s pure mind is, as I have explained, the supreme ultimate truth,
great wisdom, and great radiance; having forever severed the darkness of ignorance,
he sought bodhi in the past and has now subdued the hosts of Māra.
Having subdued those hosts of Māra, you have attained great fearlessness;
forever emerged from the world, you shall certainly achieve perfect enlightenment to become a Teacher of gods and humans, swiftly delivering all beings.
All of you who behold this shall give rise to great joy;
The Māra kings and their retinues shall no longer tread upon the banks of the Nairañjanā.
Now, by the power of this vidyā-mantra, I shall shatter those veils of affliction.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Aparājita,
with a subtle and sublime Brahma-voice, pervaded the ten directions and spoke these verses:
Tadyathā | ajitañjaye jayanti aparājite māri māramāra-vati mahāmāra-vati vijayanti vijaye sarvasiddhanamaskṛte ||
ṛtini ṛtye vidari virāpanne amari vicitre tani tre āji tre ānake āpāye varanimarase niya.
*Prāmaṇīye svāhā | Mārasainyavināśanīye svāhā | Vinayaye svāhā | Śvaṅkarīye svāhā.*
Oṃ svāhā śāntikāriye svāhā | Śrīye svāhā | Yaśomati śrīmati sarvakarmakara svāhā ||
*Niḥsarvārthasādani sarvārthapravādhani sarvamogharāsadhani manorati mahāmanorati*
Sarva-nirvāṇa-māśakti sarva-sattva-hita-karaṇi sarva-hitān-vardhaya viṇayi viṇayi mahāviṇayikye.
Riṇayaṃ praviśa mite citi meci mahāyeḍe ma me paśyantu sarvabhāga svāhā | Ṭakka svāhā | Ṭakka ci ṭakka vaḥ ||
Rāṭṭhakaṭṭha-kaṇī-gaṇavaraṇi hārīte śrīmāte tiṣṭha tiṣṭha kuṇajarīṇa mama dārmakārase nasye parivāra.
Svāhā sarvamahidani vāraya svāhā | āye naye dhye dharaye dhṛti śāśe īle mīle hīle mīle vīle līle vīle cīle bīle vīle mī ||
Līṃ līṃ līṃ kṣīlī līṃ līṃ kṣiṇi ehi āgaccha āgaccha nāgaccha tṛṣṭe tṛṣṇe tṛṣṭi sakhī varuṇi vāte indrarudra-ārjaye āroja-varuṇi.
Carmadvaya-rañja-somarañja-vijaya-bañja-somarañja-naṇḍaki-rañja-cakravijaye-rañja-vijayan-tu-rañja-durddhara-sthira-rañja.
Ākarṣaya virūḍhaka ākarṣaya virūpākṣa ākarṣaya kumbhāṇḍa ākarṣaya maṇibhadra ākarṣaya vasuki ākarṣaya prahamadāsahasrapṛthivīdevatā ākarṣaya.
Maitrīpāda-garbha-dharma svamitra-jñāna-mas-tu pañca-stoka-ya-le-le svāhā śrā-han-mi-prahan-ma-sa.
Vārī-bhūrṇi bhūrṇa-maruṭe aciva citi caṇḍike kara-kaci viṣṇu-nu mahā-viṣṇu-abhisāru mahā.
Bisāruṇḍe hūṃ huṃ huṃ huṃ supuṣpe svasti svastiraṇi naraṇi nimi nimi curuṇakale mahācuruṇakale curuṇa.
Kha-kha-le pi-ta-na-ti ma-kā-ra-na-ti i-ha-ma-nā-je vi-ha-ma-nā-je i-ha-ha-nu vi-ha-ha-nu va-hu pa-ri-ba-ri-ni-ri pa-ri-ba-ri a-na-ta pa-ri-ba-ri-ta.
Rāḷu-kīya parivāriṃ me pralaṃ me kālaṃ me kāraśca kāraśca śunari kāraśca śule biddhi me le vi-le ji-le sarva-ro-ḥ.
Ākarṣaṇīye svāhā | Sarvalokavaśaṃkarīye svāhā | Karajakaravartitisthitistha ||
Cauḥ kurañjarīṇa mamadarmakāriṇāśya sarvaparivāśya sarvahitannivārāya svāhā | Anaye anaya matye |
Bhūte bhūtādike jvalini samantapradīpani amoghe hile hile svāhā mahākāruṇike śate śate nijāye svāhā.
Ṛṇadhāraṇīyan sa-pri-se-ta-pri-te-vyañ-ja-ga-ta-saṃpanna-sarva-māra-parājaya-ghātaka-vraṇa-ti-ṛkṣe.
Hūṃ hūṃ dṛṅ gṛhṇa vāraṇa dṛśyaṇa dṛśya śira-vāraṇa tiṣṭha tiṣṭha dāraya jvalita-mahākara-sena svāhā.
Parivārasarvahitānīvarāya svāhā | Arkir arkiḥ sattare sattare hile hile dhani mani nanat ||
Kinnaraṇa kinnakurumu kurusvāhā | cakravartipraveśa mahācakravartipraveśa sūtrāntapraveśa mahāsūtrāntapraveśa ||
Samanta-praveśa karaṇa, samanta-praveśa mahākaraṇa, samanta-praveśa jikha vaṃ,
samanta-praveśa mahājikha vaṃ, samanta-praveśa kāyana, samanta-praveśa mahākāyana, samanta-praveśa kṛtāyana, samanta-praveśa...
mahā-gṛhṇa-jvālā-praviśa-narāja-ne-vānāṃ praviśa-samudra-rājana-kṣatrarāṇaṃ praviśa-varuṇi-ku-rajanam.
Oṃ namo bhagavate aparājita-buddhi-sampanna-kāya-namo-bhūte. At that time, the Bodhisattva Aparājita...
Having subdued the Māra king and his retinue,
and having brought both principle and phenomena to completion with his vows fully realized, he became a Great Compassionate Teacher.
At that time, he spoke this dhāraṇī.
Tadyathā: dhu-bu dhu-bu dhuru dhuru dhūmu dhūmu īru-cī īru-cī īru-cī viru-cī viru-cī viru-cī iru-buru śiṅkara piṅgale naṭa naṭari tu-ru tu-ri hi-hi hi-hi ni vavari ni vavari yudha-zari yudha-za.
Riṃ taniṇi ahamehame khagaca rikiṭikiṭi kiṭikiṭi budha gṛhṇa mama maheśvari mardaya mardaya mardaya nase nase nase nase nase dāri dāri dūri dūri hana me hame varaṃ vāri.
Varaya pūjara pūjari jvara-pannaniye kuru kucikāni kāni ghanavarani hu hu hu hu kuru kuṇi kuru sabhane kṣīriṇi karase marase urijandhari caṇḍale maṇḍe jyurule bumakṣe mraḥ.
Hammāṇi naṭani traṇaśaye trīpūrakiśriṇi svāhā | Traṇavinarāṇi siddhaye svāhā | Tadyathā | hile hile natiśya naṭavipunarajaṃ vidyām ||
Naraye Mivaruṇisumahānidhite Svāhā | Yadu Vidyut-gata-sūryāya Tārasurya-vyudgata-jvalana-sūryānāmase Diti-tacchi-proktaratna ||
dviparivarto mṛgaśramaṇa-namo-hi-dhanu-cakru-cakrin-dariye-namo-hi-asuri-namo-hi-dhanu-cakru-cakru-buddha-saddharmo-hi-rākṣasa-se-namo-hi-dhanu-cakru-cakru-sthai-śca-mo.
By the power of the great mantra *hīṃ daṃ ta*,
he caused the hosts of Brahmā, as well as the śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas, [to be subdued].
The multitudes of all worlds— devas, humans, and asuras—
shall never again behold the realms of the māras;
furthermore, this mantra is able to provide protection and refuge.
It benefits sentient beings, pacifies calamities and afflictions,
and neutralizes all poisons so that they may attain peace and happiness.
Whether it be humans, non-humans, the multitude of devas, the assembly of devas, or the assembly of devīs—
Asuras and the hosts of asuras, as well as the hosts of asura women;
gandharvas and the hosts of gandharvas, as well as the hosts of gandharva women;
nāgas and the hosts of nāgas, as well as the hosts of nāga women.
Yakṣas and hosts of yakṣas, as well as hosts of yakṣīs;
rākṣasas and hosts of rākṣasas, as well as hosts of rākṣasīs;
piśācas and hosts of piśācas, as well as hosts of piśācīs.
The bhūtas and the hosts of bhūtas, and the bhūta-women and their hosts;
the kaṭapūtanas and the hosts of kaṭapūtanas, and the kaṭapūtana-women and their hosts.
Caryā, Caryā, and the assembly of Caryās and the assembly of Caryā women;
Umānā, Umānā, and the assembly of Umānās and the assembly of Umānā women;
Abhramā, Abhramā, and the assembly of Abhramās and the assembly of Abhramā women.
Oṣṭrā and oṣṭrā hosts, as well as oṣṭrī hosts; gṛha and gṛha hosts, as well as gṛhī hosts.
The Karkinas, the hosts of Karkinas, and the female Karkina hosts;
furthermore, there are vetālas and black bhūtas.
The *jvarāṇuyūveḍani* [spirits], the spirits of poisonous drugs, the spirits of pustular diseases,
the spirits of ulcerous diseases, the spirits of leprosy, the spirits of choking diseases, and the spirits of vomiting diseases.
When those possessed and bewitched by various demons— such as the deluding demons of perversion, the demons of folly,
those with malicious intent, and those with wrathful intent— [are afflicted].
None of these can cause harm; in the end, they find no opportunity.
This power of the Great Radiance cannot be burned by fire, cannot be swept away by water, and cannot be injured by poison.
Swords, staves, bows, and arrows cannot harm them;
wicked thieves and bandits cannot terrify them;
sudden illnesses do not invade them, their lives are not cut short prematurely, and they enjoy a long and enduring lifespan.
All sentient beings who see him are harmonious and compliant;
all living beings who see him cherish and delight in him, and his fame spreads far and wide.
Even if they were enemies, they would treat him as brothers.
May all the various benefits previously described be fully attained. To explain this: *Namaḥ sarvabuddhadharmasaṃghāyāya*.
SIDDHYA DHARMAPARĀJITAVINYASA MAMADARMAKARAṆE SVĀHĀ SARVABHŪTĀNĀM ANARTHAPRATIVIDHVAṄGE.
Āḥ ṭi-ṣya-saṃdarśaya svāhā mama dārikāṃ kṣipraṃ sārvabhautika-siddhivinyase.
The Sūtra of the Great Dhāraṇī Mantra of Aparājita (Invincible) Svāhā.
